newsitem.title: FRANCE: Audit to show how deficit worsened in H1 - S-Kahn.
newsitem.headline: Audit to show how deficit worsened in H1 - S-Kahn.

text.p: French Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn said on Tuesday an audit of public finances would be ready by July 21 and that it was likely to show the deficit had worsened.

"Everything points to the budget which you (opposition parties) voted will not be fulfilled.... The prime minister said the situation was serious, and it is," Strauss-Kahn said in the National Assembly.
"During the election campaign we promised not to worsen the deficit, but, unfortunately it has, because of your (opposition centre-right) own decisions in the first half of the year," he said.
Strauss-Kahn said the audit report on public finances "will be submitted on July 21".
"It goes without saying that this report will be made public immediately," the new Socialist finance minister said during question time in the lower house of parliament.

"As a result (of what the audit reveals) the spending that we will want to undertake will be weighted against a certain number of spending commitments that we will not make. This reflects our priorities," he said.

Socialist Prime Minister Lionel Jospin reiterated during the same question session that his new government had managed at the Amsterdam EU summit to get jobs and growth pushed higher up the EU agenda alongside budget stability.

"In this very short space of time we tried to put things right, and alongside the legitimate demands of budget stability and monetary rigour, to introduce other, broader prospects concerning employment, growth and coordination of economic policies."
